Altman (1995) Z''-score: 6.56*(WC/TA) + 3.26*(RE/TA) + 6.72*(EBIT/TA) + 1.05*(book equity/TL); emerging-markets/non-manufacturer variant using book equity (no market price input) and operating income as the EBIT proxy.
citation: Altman, E.I., Hartzell, J. & Peck, M. (1995), "Emerging Markets Corporate Bonds: A Scoring System", Salomon Brothers.

definition: Piotroski (2000) F-score: nine year-over-year binary fundamental-strength signals (4 profitability, 3 funding/liquidity, 2 efficiency) summed 0-9.
citation: Piotroski, J.D. (2000), "Value Investing: The Use of Historical Financial Statement Information to Separate Winners from Losers", Journal of Accounting Research, 38 (Supplement), pp. 1-41.

definition: Ohlson (1980) O-score: nine-term bankruptcy-probability logit (GNP-deflator term omitted; a rank-preserving additive shift).
citation: Ohlson, J.A. (1980), "Financial Ratios and the Probabilistic Prediction of Bankruptcy", Journal of Accounting Research, 18(1), pp. 109-131.

definition: Beneish (1999) eight-variable M-score for earnings-manipulation risk (DSRI, GMI, AQI, SGI, DEPI, SGAI, TATA, LVGI).
citation: Beneish, M.D. (1999), "The Detection of Earnings Manipulation", Financial Analysts Journal, 55(5), pp. 24-36.

definition: 3-way DuPont ROE decomposition: net profit margin (NI/Revenue) x asset turnover (Revenue/Assets) x equity multiplier (Assets/Equity); telescopes to the same value as return_on_equity (NI/Equity), an identity check on the decomposition.
citation: Brealey, R.A., Myers, S.C. & Allen, F., "Principles of Corporate Finance" (DuPont identity, financial ratio analysis chapter).

definition: 5-way extended DuPont ROE decomposition: tax burden (NI/Pretax Income) x interest burden (Pretax Income/EBIT) x operating margin (EBIT/Revenue) x asset turnover (Revenue/Assets) x leverage (Assets/Equity); uses operating income as the EBIT proxy. Telescopes to the same NI/Equity identity as roe_dupont_3way.
citation: Brealey, R.A., Myers, S.C. & Allen, F., "Principles of Corporate Finance" (extended/5-way DuPont decomposition, financial ratio analysis chapter).

definition: EBITDA (operating income plus depreciation and amortization) divided by interest expense.
citation: Graham, B. & Dodd, D., "Security Analysis" (fixed-charge/interest coverage tests, credit-analysis chapter); Moody's Investors Service rating-methodology EBITDA/Interest coverage ratio.

definition: Operating cash flow plus interest expense plus income tax expense (cash paid for interest and taxes added back to OCF), divided by interest expense -- a cash-basis coverage measure.
citation: Graham, B. & Dodd, D., "Security Analysis" (cash-basis fixed-charge coverage, credit-analysis chapter); Moody's Investors Service rating-methodology (CFO before interest and taxes)/Interest coverage ratio.

definition: Sloan (1996) total accruals, cash-flow-statement operationalization: (net income - operating cash flow) divided by average total assets. Higher accruals signal a larger gap between reported earnings and cash generation.
citation: Sloan, R.G. (1996), "Do Stock Prices Fully Reflect Information in Accruals and Cash Flows About Future Earnings?", The Accounting Review, 71(3), pp. 289-315; operationalization per Hribar, P. & Collins, D.W. (2002), "Errors in Estimating Accruals: Implications for Empirical Research", Journal of Accounting Research, 40(1), pp. 105-134.

definition: Sloan (1996) working-capital accruals, balance-sheet operationalization: [(change in current assets - change in cash) - change in current liabilities] divided by average total assets. NOTE: Sloan's original formula nets change in current liabilities against change in short-term debt and change in income taxes payable (dCL - dSTD - dTP); this warehouse has no short-term-debt or taxes-payable item registered (documented S4-2 input gap), so the full change in current liabilities is used unadjusted -- a conservative, documented deviation from the exact published formula.
citation: Sloan, R.G. (1996), "Do Stock Prices Fully Reflect Information in Accruals and Cash Flows About Future Earnings?", The Accounting Review, 71(3), pp. 289-315 (equation 1, balance-sheet approach; dSTD/dTP terms omitted per the documented S4-2 input gap).

definition: Days Sales Outstanding: (average accounts receivable / revenue) x 365.
citation: Brigham, E.F. & Ehrhardt, M.C., "Financial Management: Theory & Practice" (cash-conversion-cycle chapter).

definition: Days Inventory Outstanding: (average inventory / cost of revenue) x 365.
citation: Brigham, E.F. & Ehrhardt, M.C., "Financial Management: Theory & Practice" (cash-conversion-cycle chapter).

definition: Days Payables Outstanding: (average accounts payable / cost of revenue) x 365.
citation: Brigham, E.F. & Ehrhardt, M.C., "Financial Management: Theory & Practice" (cash-conversion-cycle chapter).

definition: Cash Conversion Cycle: Days Sales Outstanding + Days Inventory Outstanding - Days Payables Outstanding (days cash is tied up in the operating cycle).
citation: Brigham, E.F. & Ehrhardt, M.C., "Financial Management: Theory & Practice" (cash-conversion-cycle chapter).

definition: Trailing basic earnings per share: TTM net income divided by weighted-average basic shares outstanding.
citation: FASB ASC 260, Earnings Per Share (basic EPS = income available to common shareholders / weighted-average common shares outstanding).

definition: Trailing diluted earnings per share: TTM net income divided by weighted-average diluted shares outstanding.
citation: FASB ASC 260, Earnings Per Share (diluted EPS = income available to common shareholders / weighted-average diluted common shares outstanding).

definition: Revenue divided by shares outstanding.
citation: Fridson, M.S. & Alvarez, F., "Financial Statement Analysis: A Practitioner's Guide" (per-share metrics chapter).

definition: Operating cash flow divided by shares outstanding.
citation: Fridson, M.S. & Alvarez, F., "Financial Statement Analysis: A Practitioner's Guide" (per-share metrics chapter).

definition: Free cash flow (operating cash flow plus signed capex) divided by shares outstanding.
citation: Fridson, M.S. & Alvarez, F., "Financial Statement Analysis: A Practitioner's Guide" (per-share metrics chapter).

definition: Tangible book value per share: (stockholders' equity - goodwill - other intangible assets) divided by shares outstanding.
citation: Fridson, M.S. & Alvarez, F., "Financial Statement Analysis: A Practitioner's Guide" (tangible book value construction).

definition: Montier (2008) C-score: six binary earnings-quality/manipulation red flags summed 0-6 (widening NI-OCF gap, rising receivable days, rising inventory days, rising other-current-assets share, declining depreciation rate, total asset growth over 10%).
citation: Montier, J. (2008), "Cooking the Books, or, More Sailing Under the Black Flag", Societe Generale Cross Asset Research (Global Equity Strategy), 6 June 2008.

definition: Market capitalization divided by trailing-twelve-month net income.
Market capitalization divided by stockholders' equity.
Market capitalization divided by trailing-twelve-month revenue.
Enterprise value: market capitalization plus long-term debt minus cash and equivalents.
Enterprise value divided by EBITDA, where EBITDA is operating income plus depreciation and amortization.
Enterprise value divided by trailing-twelve-month revenue.
Free cash flow yield: operating cash flow plus signed capital expenditures divided by market capitalization.
Trailing-twelve-month net income divided by market capitalization.
Absolute trailing-twelve-month dividends paid divided by market capitalization.
